name: Master of Graphic and Communication Design
description: This two-year course builds skill in typography, layout, identity systems and visual storytelling. Students work through studio briefs, critique sessions and a major self-directed project that is shown to an invited panel at the end.

name: Master of Interaction Design
description: A one-year course in designing screens, flows and the small behaviours inside software. You learn to sketch, prototype and test with real users, then refine what you built from what they did rather than what they said.

name: Master of Animation and Visual Effects
description: Over two years you learn character animation, compositing and the pipelines used to move a shot from storyboard to final frame. Teaching is mostly in the lab and in small production teams, with a short film or effects reel as the finishing work.

name: Diploma of Digital Media Design
description: A short practical course for people starting out in digital design. You make posters, simple websites and short videos, and learn the software and the habits of working to a brief.

name: Master of Game Design and Development
description: This course treats games as designed systems. Students prototype mechanics, write level documents, balance rules through play-testing and build a playable game in a team over the second year. Programming is taught as a design tool, not as the main aim.

name: Master of Photography and Visual Media
description: A one-year course for people who want to make photographic and moving-image work with a clear point of view. Students shoot, edit and sequence series of images, and discuss each other's work in weekly seminars.

name: Master of Design Research
description: For designers who want to ask better questions about their own field. The two years cover research methods, writing, and a long practice-led project, which is examined with a written exegesis and an exhibition.

name: Master of Industrial and Product Design
description: A two-year course where students take a product from a rough idea to a working prototype. You draw, model in clay and cad, test with users, and learn how materials and manufacturing choices shape what can be made.

name: Master of Architecture
description: A studio-based course that carries students from site analysis to a fully resolved building design. Lectures on structure, environment and law support the studio, and the second year is given to a single design thesis.

name: Master of Interior Architecture
description: The course teaches how to reshape existing buildings for new uses. You study space planning, lighting, joinery and materials, and present proposals through drawings, models and written rationale.

name: Master of Visual Communication and Branding
description: In one year this course takes students through naming, identity, packaging and the written guidelines that keep a brand consistent. Most of the work is done in response to briefs from outside organisations.

name: Diploma of Graphic Design Practice
description: A one-year diploma that gets you making real design work quickly. You learn layout, colour, type and print preparation, and put together a small portfolio by the end.

name: Master of Animation and Digital Storytelling
description: Students write, board and animate short narrative pieces in both hand-drawn and computer-built styles. The first year builds craft and the second year is spent producing one longer film with a small crew, drawing on scripting and sound design.

name: Master of Fashion and Textile Design
description: This course combines pattern making, textile printing and garment construction with a good deal of research into materials. Students build a small collection over the second year and write about the thinking behind it.

name: Master of Design Innovation
description: This course asks students to tackle open problems with design methods such as interviews, mapping, prototyping and testing. Work is done in teams across two years, with a final project built around a partner organisation.

name: Master of Architecture and Urban Design
description: A course joining building design with the study of streets, blocks and public space. Students learn through studios on real city sites, helped by units on planning policy, transport and landscape.

name: Master of Service Design and Innovation
description: A one-year course on how to design a service from the customer's side and the staff's side at once. Students map journeys, run co-design workshops and prototype whole services, then test them in the field.

name: Master of Visual Communication
description: The course covers information design, illustration, typography and image-making across print and screen. Students move from short exercises to a large practice project and discuss it in regular peer review.

name: Diploma of Interior Design and Decoration
description: A year of practical training in drafting rooms, choosing finishes and presenting a scheme to a client. Students draw by hand and on screen, and finish with a complete residential interior proposal.

name: Master of Digital Experience Design
description: Students design and test apps, websites and connected products for a one-year course. The emphasis falls on user research, interface patterns and accessibility, and each student ends with a case study of a product designed from first sketch to working prototype.

name: Master of Landscape Architecture
description: This course trains students to design parks, streets and open spaces. Plants, water, soil and climate are studied alongside drawing and modelling, and the studios work on real sites around the city.

name: Master of Design (Communication Design)
description: This two-year course sharpens skills in visual communication, from identity and publication to campaign work. Students learn by solving briefs in the studio, writing about their decisions and presenting to visiting designers.

name: Master of Design Thinking and Service Innovation
description: A one-year course that brings design methods into how organisations plan and deliver services. You interview users and staff, map what happens behind the counter and test small changes with real customers before recommending larger ones.

name: Master of Industrial Design
description: Teaching centres on designing physical products for people. You sketch, model and test objects at increasing scale, learn how things are made and finish with a prototype that has been tried by real users.

name: Master of Animation
description: A studio course where students develop a personal style in animation and then apply it to a team production. Subjects include character performance, background design, sound and editing, and the final year is spent on one short film.

name: Diploma of Graphic Design
description: A hands-on diploma for beginners in graphic design. You are taught the principles of layout and image, then use them to produce a logo, a poster series and a small publication.

name: Master of Games and Interactive Design
description: Students design games, installations and interactive pieces, using engines and physical sensors. The course puts weight on prototyping quickly, watching people play and rewriting the design after that.

name: Master of Architecture (Design)
description: This course gives a professional grounding in architectural design. Studios deal with housing, civic buildings and sites that are hard to build on, while theory units cover how architecture is argued about and documented.

name: Master of Design and Visual Arts
description: A course where design and fine art practice meet. Students make work in print, digital and object forms, write about their influences and exhibit a body of work in the second year.

name: Master of Architecture and Design
description: A studio-led architecture course placed in a region with strong landscape and timber building traditions. Students design small buildings for real sites, build full-size details and finish with a thesis on a topic of their own choosing.

name: Master of Interaction and Web Design
description: One year of work on designing and building websites and small web apps. You learn layout, front-end code, content structure and testing with users, and complete a live project for a community client.

name: Diploma of Design Foundations
description: An entry course that introduces the main design disciplines, so students can find out where they fit. You try drawing, graphic layout, object making and basic digital tools, and finish with a portfolio.

name: Master of Landscape and Urban Design
description: The course trains designers to work on coasts, towns and rural places. Students survey sites, draw plans and sections, and propose changes that deal with water, plants and the people who use the place.

name: Master of Product and Furniture Design
description: Students design and make furniture and household objects, mainly in timber. The workshop is central, and drawing, joinery and finishing are taught alongside the thinking about use and long-term wear.

name: Master of Design (Visual Communication)
description: A studio course in visual communication across print, screen and space. Students work on short briefs first, then on one large project that they define with a supervisor, and finish with a published portfolio.

name: Master of Experience and Service Design
description: A two-year course for designing services that people use across several channels. Students research users, draw journey maps and service blueprints, then prototype and trial them with a partner such as a council or a clinic.

name: Master of Industrial Design (Product)
description: In this course students design products with a clear function and manufacturable form. You build models by hand and on screen, study how people hold and use things, and produce a pre-production prototype in the second year.

name: Master of Architecture (Professional)
description: The course continues a student's architectural education through design studios, building technology and practice management. Work moves from precise small briefs towards one large building design, with regular reviews by practising architects.

name: Diploma of Digital Design and Animation
description: A diploma for those who want to start animating and designing for screens. You draw, learn timing, build simple three-dimensional scenes and put together a short animated piece.

name: Master of Interaction and Information Design
description: This one-year course is about making complex information easy to use. Students design dashboards, maps, forms and diagrams, test them with readers and revise them until people can use them without help.

name: Master of Creative Industries Design
description: A flexible one-year course for designers working in publishing, events, exhibitions and screen. Students pick a set of studios in their area and add units on pitching, budgets and managing a creative project.

name: Master of Interaction Design and Electronic Arts
description: Students design interactive media for screens, public spaces and the body. The studios blend programming, sensor work and visual design, and the second year is given to a long self-directed project that is shown in public.

name: Master of Industrial Design (Monash)
description: A course on designing manufactured products for use, repair and recycling. Students draw, model and test their designs in studios and workshops, and learn how engineers and makers handle a design afterwards.

name: Master of Architecture and Urban Design (Monash)
description: A long design studio course on buildings and the settings around them. Units on climate, structure and urban theory support the studios, and the second year is a thesis on a topic that students propose.

name: Master of Communication Design
description: A course that covers how messages are designed for different audiences, from posters and books to apps and exhibition spaces. Students develop a strong portfolio through studio briefs and a long final project.

name: Master of Service Design
description: A one-year course in designing services that work for the people who deliver and receive them. Methods taught include contextual interviews, service blueprinting, co-design and pilot testing, and students apply them to a live organisation.

name: Diploma of Creative Technology Design
description: A diploma that links design to small amounts of code and electronics. Students make interactive posters, simple games and light-up objects, learning how to get a sketch running on a screen or a circuit board.

name: Master of Fashion Design and Technology
description: Students design clothing and learn about the technology that goes with it, such as digital pattern making, knitting machines and low-waste cutting. A first-year grounding is followed by a collection developed with a supervisor.

name: Master of Design (Digital Design)
description: Students learn to design websites, apps and digital campaigns, with attention to the way people read and act on screens. Studio work is mixed with units on research and writing, and ends in a large project built for an outside client.

name: Master of Architecture (Deakin)
description: A professional architecture course built around studios and construction knowledge. Students draw and model buildings, test them against codes and climate, and complete a design thesis in the final semester.

name: Master of Animation and Visual Effects (Deakin)
description: The course trains students in the whole production path of animation and effects. They model, rig and animate, then composite, light and render, working in teams under real deadlines.

name: Master of Industrial and Product Design (Deakin)
description: A one-year course for graduates who want to move into physical product design. You practise sketching, three-dimensional modelling and user testing, and complete a project that takes an idea to a tested prototype.

name: Diploma of Graphic Design and Illustration
description: A one-year diploma that combines graphic layout with illustration. Students draw by hand and on tablets, and use the images they make in posters, books and web pages.

name: Master of Experience Design
description: This one-year course teaches how to shape what a person feels and does while using a product, a space or a service. Students conduct interviews, make storyboards and prototypes, and test them in short cycles.

name: Master of Game Art and Design
description: Teaching in this course covers concept art, three-dimensional modelling, level layout and game feel. Students collaborate in small teams to build a game, and each person is responsible for a clear part of the work.

name: Diploma of Graphic Design
description: A practical diploma where students work on layouts, logos and print jobs from the first week. Teachers are working designers, and the year closes with a small portfolio shown to the class.

name: Diploma of Interior Design and Decoration
description: Students learn to plan rooms, pick colours and finishes, and present a scheme in drawings and sample boards. Classes are small and practical, and the year includes a residential design project for a model client.

name: Diploma of Digital Media Design
description: Over two years students learn to make websites, short videos and animated graphics. The first year builds software skills and the second is spent on work-ready projects, such as a small site built for a local group.

name: Diploma of Animation
description: A two-year diploma that moves from drawing and timing to short animated films. Students study movement, character and storytelling, and finish with a short film made with a small group.

name: Diploma of Fashion Design and Technology
description: Students sketch, cut patterns and sew garments from simple to complex. The course also teaches fabrics, fittings and how to present a small range at the end of the year.

name: Diploma of Service Design
description: An entry course to service design, where students learn to map a customer's path through a service and find where it fails. They run simple interviews, draw journey maps and suggest changes to a real local service.

name: Diploma of Furniture Design and Making
description: A workshop course in which students design furniture, then build it. Over two years they learn timber, joinery, finishing and drawing, and develop a small collection to sell or exhibit.

name: Diploma of Photo Imaging
description: Students shoot and edit photographs in the studio and on location. They learn lighting, camera control and image editing, and finish with a portfolio of images for print and web.
